rubric_intent: Score the engineering substance of a marketing document for an AI observability platform

dimensions.name: Technical Specificity of Observability Scope
dimensions.description: Measures whether the description names concrete, observable engineering signals (e.g., latency percentiles, token-level drift, inference queue depth) rather than vague terms like 'visibility' or 'performance'.
dimensions.evidence_instructions: Scan all text for nouns and phrases that denote measurable system attributes; count occurrences of domain-specific, quantifiable metrics (e.g., 'p95 latency', 'OOM rate', 'KV cache hit ratio') vs. generic abstractions ('performance', 'reliability', 'insight'); zero instances of concrete signals is weak evidence.

dimensions.name: Architecture-Exposed Differentiation
dimensions.description: Measures whether the description references distinctive, engineering-relevant architectural choices (e.g., sidecar instrumentation, async telemetry batching, model-level tracing) that explain *how* observability is achieved.
dimensions.evidence_instructions: Look for proper nouns or technical constructs implying implementation decisions (e.g., 'eBPF-based capture', 'schema-on-read telemetry ingestion', 'per-pipeline span propagation'); absence of any architecture-adjacent terms beyond 'cloud-native stack' is weak evidence.

dimensions.name: AI-Workload Specificity
dimensions.description: Measures whether the description names challenges or signals unique to AI/ML systems (e.g., prompt degradation, embedding drift, GPU memory fragmentation) rather than generic SaaS or infra observability concerns.
dimensions.evidence_instructions: Identify terms tied to AI lifecycle stages (preprocessing, inference, fine-tuning) or ML-specific failure modes (e.g., 'logit collapse', 'RAG retrieval latency', 'batch size throttling'); 'model performance' without qualification is insufficient.

dimensions.name: Operational Precision of Value Claims
dimensions.description: Measures whether value propositions (e.g., 'instant visibility') are anchored to engineering outcomes with measurable scope, latency, or fidelity (e.g., 'sub-second p99 trace tail sampling', 'per-token cost attribution').
dimensions.evidence_instructions: Examine adverbs and modifiers attached to benefit claims ('instant', 'real-time', 'granular'); check if they are qualified by engineering constraints (e.g., 'within 200ms', 'at batch level', 'with <1% sampling bias'); unqualified superlatives score low.

dimensions.name: Instrumentation Transparency
dimensions.description: Measures whether the description indicates *what* must be instrumented, *how* (e.g., SDK, OpenTelemetry exporter, auto-inject), or *what’s inferred* vs. *what’s measured*.
dimensions.evidence_instructions: Search for verbs or nouns indicating integration mechanics (e.g., 'auto-instrumented LLM wrappers', 'OpenTelemetry collector plugin', 'inference log parsing'); 'built on cloud-native stack' alone provides no observable evidence.

dimensions.name: Failure Mode Coverage
dimensions.description: Measures whether the description acknowledges or enables detection of AI-specific operational failures (e.g., hallucination spikes, context window overflow, tokenizer mismatch).
dimensions.evidence_instructions: Look for named failure conditions or anti-patterns (e.g., 'prompt injection detection', 'KV cache thrashing alerts', 'output length truncation monitoring'); generic terms like 'reliability' without failure semantics are insufficient.
